segments.text: There it is.
The Rocca.
When I was given the commission, a twelfth-century tower already stood on top of the hill: the Torre di Santa Maria.
I could have demolished it and started again.
But a good architect must also recognise what can be reused.
So I incorporated it into the new fortification and made it the keep: the most secure heart of the Rocca.
Work began in fourteen thirty-five.
The principle I followed was simple: a fortress shouldn't rely on a single line of defence to keep it safe.
If the enemy got through the first entrance, they reached the courtyard.
If they took the courtyard, the defenders could make the staircase up to the wall walk unusable.
And if they advanced further still, the keep's drawbridge could be raised, cutting the tower off completely.
A fortress within a fortress.
The keep even had its own cistern and could store enough provisions to hold out for longer.
Every space was connected to the others.
But, when necessary, it could be cut off from them.
I didn't design this Rocca to be comfortable.
I designed it to be difficult to conquer.
I've discovered, though, that today it's a much more welcoming and lively place.
Not just for tourists and enthusiasts who want to learn about my work, but also for people coming to concerts, performances and evening visits.
People who climb all the way up here not to besiege the Rocca, but to spend an evening in it.
I'm told the town even hosts a music festival called Rocca'n'Roll.
I have to admit that a fortress able to withstand weapons and, centuries later, modern music has certainly proved its sound construction.
And then there's the Festa Medievale.
Every year, on the first weekend in September, the town fills once again with torches, flags, costumed performers, musicians, duels and taverns.
For a few evenings, Vicopisano sets out to recreate the atmosphere of the medieval town.
I'd be very curious to see the next edition.
I could check how faithful the reconstruction is.
And perhaps offer a few suggestions.
Only if asked, of course.
Knowing that these streets fill with people again, and that the Rocca opens at night too, makes me realise something.
A building can go on living in ways its architect never imagined.
I designed these walls to keep people out.
Today, people are welcomed and invited in.
Now let's leave the Rocca and carry on.
Our next stop will be the Torre dell'Orologio, the Clock Tower.
